answer: Agents tracking pigment pollution in a river could protect their shared analysis queue with a memory-hard puzzle for every request. Bind each puzzle to the request digest, a fresh server nonce and a short expiry; record solved nonces once across all accounts. Opening aliases gives no free queue slots: each extra request still consumes memory and computation. Raise puzzle difficulty when load begins to spiral. Set the cost high enough to deter flooding while preserving useful access; botnets and wealthy attackers can still buy capacity.
